planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in early spring and install a sturdy multi-wire trellis at planting time, since the long trailing canes will not support themselves.

directions: Chehalem is a USDA-ARS trailing blackberry bred and released in Oregon, historically significant chiefly as one of the two parent cultivars — together with Olallie — used in the 1945 cross that produced the modern benchmark cultivar Marion. Like Marion, it carries long, thorny trailing canes and ripens firm, richly flavored fruit, though it has been almost entirely eclipsed in commercial plantings by its more celebrated offspring and by later thornless USDA-ARS releases. Plant dormant canes in early spring against a sturdy multi-wire trellis, since the sprawling growth habit will not support itself. Cut spent floricanes to the ground after harvest and train the current season's primocanes onto the wires to bear next year's crop.
sources: Oregon State University Extension — Caneberry Production Guide
